title: llama.cpp vs vLLM: Which One Actually Scales? ⚡
fb_caption:
llama.cpp vs vLLM: Which Architecture Actually Scales in Production? ⚡

- Throughput: vLLM often leads due to PagedAttention, while llama.cpp excels in single-device, low-latency scenarios.
- Latency: llama.cpp can offer lower latency for smaller models/batches on consumer hardware.
- Consistency: vLLM's attention mechanisms generally provide more consistent performance under varying loads.
- Failure Modes: llama.cpp can be more prone to OOM errors without careful memory management; vLLM's batching can mask some issues but introduce its own.
- Operational Overhead: llama.cpp is simpler to deploy for edge/local, vLLM requires more robust infrastructure for production.

Recommendation: For true production scaling and high throughput, vLLM is generally the superior choice. llama.cpp shines in research, prototyping, and resource-constrained environments.
